title: Systems with simple rules and complex behavior are very common in nature

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Systems with simple rules and complex behavior are very common in nature

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because nature is not constrained to predictable designs, systems whose simple rules produce complex behavior, like rule 30 and rule 110, are very common in nature.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: one of the important conclusions of this book is that such systems are actually very common in nature.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “The Need for a New Intuition” (from p. 39), p. 40. Scope: natural systems generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.29

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Some natural systems can be tested using existing time series, but available observations are highly selective and often lack causal resolution. They cannot establish prevalence across nature as stated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a representative sample of natural systems, infer compact local rules from time-resolved observations, and quantify whether those rules generate high-complexity trajectories. Compare prevalence against a prespecified threshold and against non-program mechanistic models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Inferred simple rules are model-dependent.

Very common has no stated prevalence threshold.

No representative inventory of natural systems exists.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.35
data existence: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.25
data adequacy: 0.15
analysis feasibility: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A frequency claim about nature needs a sample of actual rules. What exists publicly is a scattering of morphological case studies and a few systems, such as some growth and pigmentation patterns, whose mechanisms are partly known. Those materials can test a short list of examples and do not estimate how common the phenomenon is.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Draw a sample of natural systems with identified microscopic rules and estimate the fraction whose rules are simple and whose behavior is complex in the sense of rule 30 or rule 110. The claim is confirmed if that fraction is high on a pre-registered cutoff, and refuted if identified natural rules are rarely of that kind.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Very common needs a denominator over natural systems that has not been defined.

Known rules of natural systems are few, and pattern resemblance is a weak proxy for those rules.
